question: Should the accepted Dreaming scope API be per-agent `agents.list[].dreaming`, a memory-core global allowlist such as `dreaming.agents`, staggered offsets, or a split where allowlist/disable lands first and scheduling is tracked separately?
rationale: This changes user-facing config, strict schema, generated docs, and which agent memory artifacts are written during upgrades; automation cannot choose the permanent config contract or schedule semantics safely.

options.title: Land allowlist first
options.body: Accept a memory-core `dreaming.agents` allowlist as the minimum durable scope control, keep existing global schedule behavior, and track per-agent scheduling or stagger offsets separately.

options.title: Use per-agent blocks
options.body: Require the implementation to model `agents.list[].dreaming` so enablement and future schedules live next to other agent overrides, at the cost of a larger config/schema change.

options.title: Defer new config surface
options.body: Pause the PRs until maintainers decide whether pressure-aware scheduling or plugin loading policy should solve the operator problem without another Dreaming config key.

recommendation.title: Land allowlist first
recommendation.body: Accept a memory-core `dreaming.agents` allowlist as the minimum durable scope control, keep existing global schedule behavior, and track per-agent scheduling or stagger offsets separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Dreaming runtime and resolver history makes this the strongest available owner signal for the product/API choice.
